title: SDO/AIA 304 Å synoptic map, Carrington rotation 2285 (June 2024)
credit: NASA/SDO and the AIA science team
note: The Sun in extreme ultraviolet light (30.4 nm), a month near the 2024 solar maximum: the bright patches are active regions. Coloured orange, as SDO shows this light; to the eye the Sun is an almost featureless white disc.

title: Mercury MESSENGER MDIS global basemap (BDR)
credit: NASA/Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory/Carnegie Institution of Washington (MESSENGER MDIS); mosaic distributed by USGS Astrogeology
note: A grey mosaic, coloured by us in Mercury's faintly brownish grey, about as bright as the Moon's map (Mercury reflects slightly more light than the Moon).

title: Mercury MESSENGER global DEM, colour shaded relief (2 km)
credit: NASA/JHUAPL/CIW (MESSENGER); elevation model and relief by USGS Astrogeology
note: Colours show height (blue low, red and white high), not what the eye sees.

title: Venus Magellan global C3-MDIR colorized topographic mosaic (6.6 km)
credit: NASA/JPL (Magellan radar); mosaic by USGS Astrogeology
note: The ground under the clouds as radar sees it, coloured by height. It is the Terrain view of Venus in the dictionary.

title: Blue Marble Next Generation, July 2004, with topography and bathymetry
credit: NASA Earth Observatory (Reto Stöckli), MODIS
note: Darks lifted (gamma 0.42, a touch more blue) so the deep oceans stay blue, not black, on a projector.

title: Earth at Night (Black Marble 2016)
credit: NASA Earth Observatory (Joshua Stevens), Suomi NPP VIIRS data from Miguel Román, NASA GSFC

title: Blue Marble clouds
credit: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center (Reto Stöckli, Robert Simmon), MODIS

title: Topography (GEBCO 2008 land elevation)
credit: NASA Earth Observatory (Reto Stöckli), from GEBCO and SRTM elevation data
note: Also gives Earth's Oceans view: everything at sea level or below.

title: Mars Viking MDIM 2.1 colour mosaic, recoloured by NASA Ames
credit: NASA/JPL (Viking Orbiters); MDIM 2.1 mosaic by USGS Astrogeology; colour by NASA Ames Research Center
note: Published colours white-balanced a little warmer (they are too blue for Mars's butterscotch).

title: Mars MGS MOLA global colour shaded relief
credit: NASA/JPL/GSFC (Mars Global Surveyor, MOLA); relief by USGS Astrogeology
note: Colours show height (blue low, red and white high), not what the eye sees.

title: Cassini's best maps of Jupiter: cylindrical map (PIA07782)
credit: NASA/JPL/Space Science Institute
note: Jupiter in December 2000. Its bands and storms drift and change, so today's Jupiter looks a little different.

title: Vesta Dawn FC global mosaic (DLR)
credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/UCLA/MPS/DLR/IDA (Dawn Framing Camera); mosaic by DLR, distributed by USGS Astrogeology
note: A grey mosaic, coloured by us.

title: Pluto New Horizons LORRI/MVIC global mosaic (300 m)
credit: NASA/Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory/Southwest Research Institute (New Horizons); mosaic by USGS Astrogeology and the New Horizons team
note: A grey mosaic, coloured by us from Sputnik Planitia's pale cream to Cthulhu's dark red-brown. New Horizons saw only the northern half well; the rest is filled in to match. Turned by 180 degrees for the app's north-side pole (see scripts/lib/iau.ts).

title: Painted cloud bands
credit: Orbitalia contributors (scripts/lib/paint.ts), after Cassini, Voyager 2 and Hubble photographs
note: Not a photograph: there is no openly licensed global map of these planets, so their bands, colours and storms are painted after spacecraft photographs (each texture's basis is in data/planet-textures.json).
